newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYOIL HIGHER ON EXPORTS, SOYMEAL MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYOIL HIGHER ON EXPORTS, SOYMEAL MIXED.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were sharply higher at midsession Tuesday, lifted in part by an increase in the forecast for U.S. exports from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, traders and analysts said.
"I think this year we will see an increase in demand from importing nations," said Mark Widner, oilseed analyst with Cargill Investor Services.

In its supply and demand forecast released Tuesday, USDA put soyoil exports for 1997/98 at 2.150 billion lbs, up from 2.050 a month ago and lowered its ending stocks forecast by 180 million lbs to 1.795 billion.
Soymeal futures were mixed, with some months under pressure from soyoil/soymeal spread trade, traders said.
"I was a little surprised that soymeal didn't receive more support from the corn," one trader said.
In early trade, Produce Grain bought 500 lots soyoil and Term Commodities bought 200 October. In soymeal trade, ADM bought 500 lots October.
At 1207 CDT, soyoil was 0.25 to 0.50 cent per lb higher, with August up 0.25 at 22.08 cents. Soymeal was $1.00 per ton lower to $1.80 higher, with August up $1.80 at $251.80 a ton.
